description: We are an international team of aerospace, computer science, data science, and mechatronics engineers coming together to find optimal Earth locations for testing future technologies and landing systems, and to simulate missions to the Moon and Mars.
summary: LUMSTEM (Lunar & Martian Surface To Earth Mapping) is a physics-informed, multi-modal planetary analog discovery engine that evaluates and ranks terrestrial testbeds for permanent Moon bases and Mars landing sites. Traditional analog selection often relies on subjective visual resemblance or single-parameter comparisons, overlooking critical environmental mismatches that cause hardware failures. LUMSTEM solves this by evaluating 320 high-resolution Earth micro-tiles (58.98 km² each) across 15 global regions against 6 official NASA reference sites (Shackleton Crater Rim, Shackleton PSR Floor, Apollo 15 Hadley Rille, Jezero Crater, Valles Marineris, and Arsia Mons). Combining AI Vision Transformer (DINOv2) geomorphology embeddings with 3D physical slope, terrain ruggedness, thermal/illumination swings, and mafic-silicate lithology, LUMSTEM delivers an interactive 3D Mission Control web interface. Researchers can dynamically weight mission priorities, activate Discovery Mode to uncover novel testbeds, and inspect an Explainable Similarity Analysis radar graph alongside explicit physical breakdown constraints (gravity, atmospheric buffering, and hydrology).
details:
1. WHAT LUMSTEM DOES & HOW IT WORKS

LUMSTEM (Lunar & Martian Surface To Earth Mapping) is a quantitative, multi-modal decision-support tool for mission planners, planetary geologists, and robotics engineers. Instead of relying on qualitative visual comparisons, LUMSTEM ingests orbital Digital Elevation Models (DEMs), thermal datasets, and geochemical indices to evaluate 320 terrestrial micro-tiles (256 × 256 pixels at 30 m resolution, covering 7.68 × 7.68 km or 58.98 km² per tile) across 15 global regions against 6 official NASA Moon and Mars reference targets:

• Moon Targets: Shackleton Crater Illuminated Rim (89.9°S), Shackleton Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) Floor (89.9°S), and Apollo 15 Hadley Rille (26.13°N, 3.63°E).

• Mars Targets: Jezero Crater Delta (18.44°N, 77.45°E), Valles Marineris — Coprates Chasma (-13.50°S, -61.00°W), and Arsia Mons Volcanic Flank (-9.20°S, -120.50°W).

Every Earth tile is scored (0–100%) against each planetary target across five orthogonal physical dimensions:

1. 2D Geomorphology (DINOv2 Vision Transformer): Extracts 384-dimensional cosine-similarity embeddings from normalized 3D elevation tensors to match landform topology (craters, sinuous rilles, canyon walls, yardang fleets).

2. Steepness / 3D Slope: Computes true physical surface inclination (degrees) using exact orbital pixel spacing (30 m Earth, 59.2 m / 118 m Moon, 200 m Mars).

3. Terrain Ruggedness (Roughness): Computes the scale-normalized standard deviation of local slope gradients, isolating local boulder/crater-wall irregularity without falsely penalizing smooth tilted slopes.

4. Thermal & 3D Illumination Regime: Combines 3D Lambertian solar grazing incidence (cos i) with NASA LRO Diviner, Mars THEMIS/MEDA, and Earth MODIS diurnal temperature swings (ΔT) and elevation lapse-rate cooling (-6.5 K/km).

5. Surface Material (Mafic-Silicate Lithology): Matches published mafic-silicate vs. evaporite geochemistry (0.15 salt pan to 0.96 tholeiitic basalt), modulated by 30 m steep-slope bedrock exposure.

2. KEY BENEFITS, CREATIVITY & INTENDED IMPACT

• Interactive 3D Planetary Globe & Synchronized Telemetry UI: Built with Three.js and Leaflet, users can orbit 3D Moon and Mars globes, click surface-locked landing site pins, and immediately inspect the top-ranked terrestrial analogs on a global satellite map.

• Dynamic Mission Weighting & Discovery Mode: Engineers testing a lunar rover can prioritize Geomorphology, Slope, and Roughness, while an ISRU drill team can prioritize Lithology and Thermal swings. Activating "Discovery Mode" filters out 7 famous, over-subscribed NASA benchmarks (e.g., Atacama, Devon Island, Askja, Hawaii, McMurdo) to uncover 8 under-utilized analog regions worldwide (e.g., Tibesti Calderas, Harrat Khaybar, Qaidam Basin, Dasht-e Lut, Danakil Depression).

• Explainable Similarity Analysis & Physical Breakdown Diagnostics: A custom SVG radar chart overlays the user's "Target Mission Profile" (slider weights) against the "Candidate Earth Site" (hatched similarity polygon) and highlights the "Verified Overlap Core" (white intersection). Crucially, the Analog Dossier explicitly warns engineers where the terrestrial analogy breaks down due to gravity differences (1.0g vs. 0.165g Moon / 0.38g Mars), atmospheric thermal buffering, and hydrological weathering.

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

• Backend Data & AI Pipeline (Python): NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Rasterio (Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF window streaming), PySTAC-Client, NASA earthaccess, and PyTorch (Meta DINOv2 ViT dinov2_vits14).

• Frontend Mission Control Web App: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Vanilla ES6 JavaScript, Three.js (r128 WebGL 3D Planetary Globe), Leaflet.js (1.9.4 Satellite Map), and custom SVG Radar Telemetry.

• Accessibility, Energy & Cost Considerations: To ensure zero barrier to entry for researchers and hackathon judges—and to avoid redundant cloud GPU energy consumption—all 1,920 tile-target evaluations are pre-computed into lightweight CSVs and compiled into an offline-ready JavaScript bundle (web/data.js) with a one-click Windows launcher (run_lumstem.bat).

4. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE

• Code & Data: Pre-trained Meta DINOv2 Vision Transformer (dinov2_vits14) was used in src/step2_vision.py to compute geomorphological similarity embeddings. Large Language Model (LLM) assistance (Google Gemini) was used to accelerate backend, frontend UI/CSS layout, SVG radar chart rendering, and documentation formatting.

• Audio & Video: The 30-second demonstration video narration was generated using SI text-to-speech synthesis (ElevenLabs) and includes a visible SI watermark on the video. No NASA logos, flags, or branding elements are used in any SI-assisted assets.
